| **US-2.9** | **As a** data engineer, **I want** silver→gold transforms orchestrated after bronze DQ success, with daily schedule, **so that** the mart refreshes every day within SLA. | Data Pipeline orchestration | FR6 |
| **Acceptance criteria** | • Dependency order: bronze → silver → gold → semantic refresh. • Rerun safe for a given business date. • Run metrics logged (rows in/out, duration). | | |

---

## Phase 3 — Semantic model & reporting
*Expose measures and visuals that satisfy FR1–FR5; refresh aligned to FR6.*

| ID | User story | Fabric / medallion | FR |
|----|------------|--------------------|-----|
| **US-3.1** | **As a** BI developer, **I want** a Fabric semantic model on gold star tables with relationships and role-playing date, **so that** reports share one governed model. | Semantic model (Direct Lake or Import on gold) | FR1–FR5 |
| **Acceptance criteria** | • Relationships: fact→dim_store, dim_product, dim_date, dim_customer, dim_promotion. • Hide key columns; mark date table. • Deployed to workspace with clear dataset name. | | |

| ID | User story | Fabric / medallion | FR |
|----|------------|--------------------|-----|
| **US-3.2** | **As a** retail analyst, **I want** measures for Units, Gross Sales, Returns, and Net Sales, **so that** I can report sales and isolate returns. | Semantic model (DAX) | FR1, FR2 |
| **Acceptance criteria** | • `Units` = sum of units (define whether returns reduce units or separate). • `Gross Sales` = sum of gross on non-return (or all) per rule. • `Returns` shown separately (amount and units). • `Net Sales` = gross − returns (FR2). • Filter context works by store, region, category, date range. | | |

| ID | User story | Fabric / medallion | FR |
|----|------------|--------------------|-----|
| **US-3.3** | **As a** retail analyst, **I want** a sales performance report by store, region, and product category for any date range, **so that** I can monitor performance. | Power BI report on semantic model | FR1, FR2 |
| **Acceptance criteria** | • Slicers: date range, region, store, category. • Visuals show units, gross, returns, net. • Drill: region → store; category → product (if in model). • Matches gold recon sample for a fixed date (± tolerance). | | |

| ID | User story | Fabric / medallion | FR |
|----|------------|--------------------|-----|
| **US-3.4** | **As a** retail analyst, **I want** all core measures split by loyalty member vs guest, **so that** I can compare enrolled shoppers to guests. | Semantic model + Power BI | FR4 |
| **Acceptance criteria** | • `dim_customer` (or equivalent) slicer/legend: Member vs Guest. • Guests = null/missing `loyalty_id` on txn. • Measures unchanged when split (totals reconcile). | | |

| ID | User story | Fabric / medallion | FR |
|----|------------|--------------------|-----|
| **US-3.5** | **As a** retail analyst, **I want** YoY and WoW comparison measures that respect ISO (or defined) weeks spanning month boundaries, **so that** trend analysis is correct. | Semantic model (DAX time intelligence) + `dim_date` | FR5 |
| **Acceptance criteria** | • WoW: current week vs prior week using week-year + week number, not calendar month. • YoY: same period prior year (day or week aligned per rule). • Week spanning two months attributes to correct week, not split incorrectly by month unless user drills by month. • Documented calendar (retail vs calendar) signed off. | | |

| ID | User story | Fabric / medallion | FR |
|----|------------|--------------------|-----|
| **US-3.6** | **As a** commercial analyst, **I want** a promotion effectiveness view (category sales in promo window vs baseline), **so that** I can judge promo lift. | Power BI + gold promo baseline + `dim_promotion` | FR3 |
| **Acceptance criteria** | • Select promo (or category + dates). • Show sales in window vs baseline period (units, gross, net). • Lift % = (promo − baseline) / baseline. • Optional: filter member vs guest (FR4). • Methodology note on baseline visible in report. | | |

| ID | User story | Fabric / medallion | FR |
|----|------------|--------------------|-----|
| **US-3.7** | **As an** analytics owner, **I want** the semantic model and reports refreshed daily after gold completes, **so that** users always see prior-day sales within SLA. | Pipeline: “Refresh semantic model” / scheduled job | FR6 |
| **Acceptance criteria** | • Refresh triggered only on gold success. • Failure alerts to ops channel. • 3 years history visible in report filters. | | |

---

## Phase 4 — Hardening & handover
*Production readiness across FR6 and trust in FR1–FR5.*

| ID | User story | Fabric / medallion | FR |
|----|------------|--------------------|-----|
| **US-4.1** | **As an** analytics owner, **I want** automated reconciliation of report totals back to bronze POS for a sample of days, **so that** FR1/FR2 numbers are trusted. | Notebook tests + Pipeline | FR1, FR2, FR6 |
| **Acceptance criteria** | • Glue check: sum(gross), count(txns), return rates bronze vs gold vs semantic. • Variances above threshold fail the run or open an incident. | | |

| ID | User story | Fabric / medallion | FR |
|----|------------|--------------------|-----|
| **US-4.2** | **As a** platform engineer, **I want** retention (3 years), access roles, and lineage documented for the Lakehouse and semantic model, **so that** operations meet FR6 and governance needs. | OneLake, Lakehouse, Power BI roles | FR6 |
| **Acceptance criteria** | • Retention job or lifecycle policy on bronze/silver/gold. • Viewer/contributor roles separated; row-level security decision recorded (if needed by region). • Runbook: daily refresh, replay date, quarantine. | | |

---

## Delivery sequence (sprint-style view)

| Sprint / phase | Focus | Primary components | Stories | FR coverage |
|----------------|--------|----------------------|---------|-------------|
| **Sprint 0** | Workspace, Lakehouse, medallion paths, ingestion framework | OneLake, Lakehouse, Pipelines | US-0.1, US-0.2 | Foundation / FR6 |
| **Sprint 1** | Bronze POS + masters + DQ | Pipelines → bronze | US-1.1–US-1.4 | FR1, FR2, FR4, FR6 |
| **Sprint 2** | Silver conform + SCD store + promo/loyalty | Dataflow Gen2 / Notebooks → silver | US-2.1–US-2.4 | FR1–FR4 |
| **Sprint 3** | Gold dims + `fact_sales` + promo assignment + orchestration | Notebooks → gold, Pipelines | US-2.5–US-2.9 | FR1–FR4, FR6 |
| **Sprint 4** | Semantic model, core sales & returns, loyalty split, daily refresh | Semantic model, Power BI | US-3.1–US-3.4, US-3.7 | FR1, FR2, FR4, FR6 |
| **Sprint 5** | YoY/WoW, promotion effectiveness, baseline | DAX, `dim_date`, promo baseline, Power BI | US-2.8 (if not done), US-3.5, US-3.6 | FR3, FR5 |
| **Sprint 6** | Recon, retention, runbooks, UAT sign-off | Notebooks, governance | US-4.1, US-4.2 | FR1–FR6 |

---

## Traceability matrix (FR → stories)

| FR | Description | Stories |
|----|-------------|---------|
| **FR1** | Sales by store, region, category, date range | US-1.1, US-1.2, US-2.1–US-2.3, US-2.5, US-2.6, US-3.1–US-3.3, US-4.1 |
| **FR2** | Returns separate; net = gross − returns | US-1.1, US-2.1, US-2.6, US-3.2, US-3.3, US-4.1 |
| **FR3** | Promotion effectiveness vs baseline | US-1.3, US-2.4, US-2.5, US-2.7, US-2.8, US-3.6 |
| **FR4** | Loyalty member vs guest | US-1.1, US-1.3, US-2.1, US-2.4, US-2.5, US-2.6, US-3.4 |
| **FR5** | YoY and WoW (weeks spanning months) | US-2.5 (`dim_date`), US-3.5 |
| **FR6** | Daily refresh; 3 years history | US-0.2, US-1.1–US-1.4, US-2.6, US-2.9, US-3.7, US-4.1, US-4.2 |

---

## Medallion & mapping cheat-sheet

```text
ADLS daily/weekly drops
        │
        ▼  Pipelines
┌───────────────────┐
│ BRONZE (raw Delta)│  pos_*, product_master, store_master, promotions, loyalty_members
└─────────┬─────────┘
          │  Dataflow Gen2 / Notebooks
┌─────────▼─────────┐
│ SILVER (conformed)│  clean POS, SCD2 store, product, promo, loyalty
└─────────┬─────────┘
          │  Notebooks (business rules + CSV mapping)
┌─────────▼─────────┐
│ GOLD (star schema)│  dim_store, dim_product, dim_promotion, dim_customer, dim_date
│                   │  fact_sales (units, gross, discount, is_return, net, promo_key)
│                   │  promo_baseline (FR3)
└─────────┬─────────┘
          │  Direct Lake / Import
┌─────────▼─────────┐
│ Semantic model    │  measures: Units, Gross, Returns, Net, WoW, YoY, Promo Lift
│ Power BI reports  │  Sales performance · Loyalty split · Promo effectiveness
└───────────────────┘
```

**CSV mapping → gold**

| Source | Target |
|--------|--------|
| `pos_lines.qty` | `fact_sales.units` |
| `pos_lines.gross_amount` | `fact_sales.gross_amount` |
| `pos_lines.discount_amount` | `fact_sales.discount_amount` |
| `pos_lines.return_flag` | `fact_sales.is_return` |
| `store_master.region` | `dim_store.region` |
| `product_master.category` | `dim_product.category` |
| `promotions.promo_id` (+ category/date range) | `dim_promotion.promotion_key` on fact |

---

### Suggested open decisions (capture in Sprint 0/2 backlog refinement)
1. **Net sales formula** — treatment of `discount_amount` vs returns (FR2).  
2. **Store region** — transaction-time (SCD2 as-of) vs current region on reports (FR1).  
3. **Promo overlap** — single promo key priority when windows overlap (FR3).  
4. **Baseline rule** — pre-period vs prior-year for promo lift (FR3).  
5. **Week definition** — ISO week vs retail 4-5-4 for WoW/YoY (FR5).  

This roadmap is sequenced so each phase only depends on the previous layer’s outputs, maps cleanly onto Fabric + medallion, and keeps FR traceability explicit on every story.

grok-4.6.text:
# Microsoft Fabric Analytics Delivery Roadmap

Medallion on **Lakehouse / OneLake** (Bronze raw → Silver conformed → Gold star schema). Ingestion via **Data Pipelines** (and shortcuts from ADLS). Transform via **Notebooks** (and Dataflow Gen2 where low-code fits). Consume via a **Fabric semantic model** + **Power BI**. Daily refresh, 3-year retain (FR6) is a cross-cutting constraint on every data-path story.

---

## Phase 1 — Platform & Bronze ingestion
*Stand up OneLake + land every source unchanged. Nothing downstream starts until Bronze is complete and scheduled.*

### US-1.1 Lakehouse & medallion folders
**As a** data platform engineer, **I want** a Fabric Lakehouse with OneLake bronze / silver / gold zones (and shortcuts to the existing ADLS landing area) **so that** all later pipelines have a single governed store and we can retain three years of history.
- **Maps to:** Lakehouse, OneLake
- **Delivers:** FR6 (foundation for all FRs)
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Lakehouse exists; `bronze/`, `silver/`, `gold/` folders (or schemas) are present.
  - ADLS landing container is shortcutted; workspace roles and OneLake data-access roles applied.
  - Retention policy documented: Bronze files kept ≥ 3 years.

### US-1.2 Ingest POS headers & lines (daily)
**As a** data engineer, **I want** a Data Pipeline that copies the daily `pos_transactions` and `pos_lines` file drops into Bronze Delta tables **so that** raw receipt grain is available the same day.
- **Maps to:** Data Pipelines → Bronze Lakehouse tables `bronze.pos_transactions`, `bronze.pos_lines`
- **Delivers:** FR1, FR2, FR4, FR5, FR6
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Pipeline triggered on file arrival (or daily schedule); idempotent (re-run does not duplicate).
  - Row counts and file-date watermark logged; schema drift fails the run.
  - `loyalty_id` remains nullable; `return_flag`, amounts, qty preserved as landed.
  - Three years of historical files backfilled.

### US-1.3 Ingest masters & reference (product, store, promotions, loyalty)
**As a** data engineer, **I want** pipelines (weekly full for product/store; full/incremental for promotions & loyalty) landing into Bronze **so that** conformed dimensions can be built without re-reading source systems.
- **Maps to:** Data Pipelines → `bronze.product_master`, `bronze.store_master`, `bronze.promotions`, `bronze.loyalty_members`
- **Delivers:** FR1, FR3, FR4, FR6
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Weekly full extract for product and store overwrites a dated Bronze snapshot (history kept).
  - Promotions and loyalty landed with source keys intact (`promo_id`, `loyalty_id`, `join_date`, `segment`).
  - Pipeline dependencies: masters complete before Silver jobs of the same cycle.

---

## Phase 2 — Silver transformation & conformance
*Clean, type, deduplicate, and apply SCD. No business facts yet — only trusted, joinable entities.*

### US-2.1 Conform POS into a single Silver sales line
**As a** analytics engineer, **I want** a Spark notebook that joins `pos_transactions` + `pos_lines`, casts types, flags returns, and writes `silver.sales_lines` **so that** Gold facts have a single clean grain (one row per receipt line).
- **Maps to:** Notebooks → Silver Delta `silver.sales_lines`
- **Delivers:** FR1, FR2, FR4, FR6
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Grain = `txn_id` + `sku` (or source line key); header attributes (`store_id`, `txn_ts`, `loyalty_id`, `channel`) denormalised onto the line.
  - `units` = `qty`; `gross_amount`, `discount_amount` carried; `is_return` derived from `return_flag`.
  - Late-arriving / duplicate files handled (merge on natural key + file date).
  - Data-quality checks: orphan lines, negative qty on non-returns, future `txn_ts` fail or quarantine.

### US-2.2 SCD Type 2 store dimension (Silver)
**As a** analytics engineer, **I want** Type-2 history on `store_master` (stores re-region) **so that** region-level sales always reflect the region that was current on the transaction date.
- **Maps to:** Notebooks → `silver.store` (effective_from / effective_to / is_current)
- **Delivers:** FR1
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Region (and format) changes open a new version; `store_id` is the durable business key.
  - Point-in-time join key available (`store_id` + date range).
  - Current-row view or flag for “as-is” reporting.

### US-2.3 Conform product, loyalty, and promotions (Silver)
**As a** analytics engineer, **I want** cleansed Silver tables for product, loyalty members, and promotions **so that** Gold dimensions and the promo date-range join have stable keys and types.
- **Maps to:** Notebooks or Dataflow Gen2 → `silver.product`, `silver.loyalty_member`, `silver.promotion`
- **Delivers:** FR1, FR3, FR4
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Product: one current row per `sku`; `category`, `brand`, `product_name` standardised.
  - Loyalty: one row per `loyalty_id`; `join_date`, `segment` typed; guests remain absent (not fabricated).
  - Promotions: `promo_id`, `category`, `promo_type`, `start_date`, `end_date` valid (`start` ≤ `end`); overlapping windows retained (not collapsed).

---

## Phase 3 — Gold dimensional model
*Star schema matching the CSV mapping. This is the only layer the semantic model reads.*

### US-3.1 Date dimension (weeks that span months)
**As a** analytics engineer, **I want** a `gold.dim_date` with calendar and ISO (or retail) week keys that do not break when a week crosses a month **so that** WoW and YoY comparisons are well-defined (FR5).
- **Maps to:** Notebooks → `gold.dim_date`
- **Delivers:** FR5 (enables FR1 date-range)
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - One row per date covering history + ≥ 1 year forward; keys: date, year, month, ISO week, week_start, week_end, prior_year_date, prior_week_date.
  - Week attributes are week-aligned (not calendar-month-aligned); a week that spans two months has a single `week_key`.
  - Documented week convention (ISO-8601 or agreed retail calendar) published to report authors.

### US-3.2 Dimensions: store, product, promotion, customer
**As a** analytics engineer, **I want** Gold dimensions `dim_store`, `dim_product`, `dim_promotion`, `dim_customer` **so that** facts can be sliced by region, category, promo, and loyalty vs guest.
- **Maps to:** Notebooks → Gold Delta tables (star)
- **Delivers:** FR1, FR3, FR4  
  *Mapping:* `store_master.region` → `dim_store.region`; `product_master.category` → `dim_product.category`; `promotions.promo_id` → `dim_promotion.promotion_key`; loyalty attributes on `dim_customer`.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - `dim_store`: surrogate key + `store_id`; Type-2 region/format; `region`, `format`, `store_name`.
  - `dim_product`: surrogate key + `sku`; `category`, `brand`, `product_name`.
  - `dim_promotion`: surrogate `promotion_key`; `promo_id`, `promo_type`, `category`, start/end.
  - `dim_customer`: surrogate key; `loyalty_id` (null = guest); `segment`, `join_date`; a dedicated **Guest** member exists for unmatched / null `loyalty_id`.
  - Unknown / not-applicable members present on every dim (no fact orphans).

### US-3.3 Fact sales (mapped grain)
**As a** analytics engineer, **I want** `gold.fact_sales` at receipt-line grain with the agreed column mapping and keys to all dimensions **so that** every sales, return, loyalty, and promo measure has a single source of truth.
- **Maps to:** Notebooks → `gold.fact_sales`
- **Delivers:** FR1, FR2, FR3, FR4, FR6  
  *Mapping:* `pos_lines.qty` → `units`; `gross_amount` → `gross_amount`; `discount_amount` → `discount_amount`; `return_flag` → `is_return`. Promo assigned by **date-range join on category + txn date**.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Grain: one row per sales line; FKs to `dim_date` (txn date), `dim_store` (PIT / Type-2 as-at txn date), `dim_product`, `dim_customer` (guest if `loyalty_id` null), `dim_promotion` (or “No promotion”).
  - Promotion assignment: `product.category = promotion.category` AND `txn_date BETWEEN start_date AND end_date`; deterministic rule when windows overlap (e.g. longest / highest-priority `promo_type`) documented and tested.
  - `net_amount` persisted or clearly derivable: gross − return gross (see FR2); return lines keep original signs/`is_return` so they can be shown separately.
  - Incremental daily merge; table holds a rolling 3-year window (FR6).
  - Reconciliation: Gold units / gross within agreed tolerance of Silver (and of Bronze sample).

---

## Phase 4 — Semantic model & measures
*One Fabric semantic model on Gold. All report logic lives here, not in visuals.*

### US-4.1 Semantic model + core sales measures
**As a** BI developer, **I want** a Fabric semantic model over the Gold star with relationships and measures for units, gross, returns, and net **so that** reports can answer FR1/FR2 without local calculations.
- **Maps to:** Semantic model (Direct Lake or Import on Gold)
- **Delivers:** FR1, FR2, FR6
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Star relationships: `fact_sales` → all dims; date is the active date relationship.
  - Measures: `Units`, `Gross Sales`, `Return Units`, `Return Gross`, `Net Sales` (= Gross − Returns) — returns shown separately from gross (FR2).
  - RLS/OLS placeholders (store/region) documented even if not enforced in v1.
  - Model refresh bound to the daily Gold pipeline (FR6); refresh failure alerts configured.

### US-4.2 Time intelligence (YoY, WoW)
**As a** sales analyst, **I want** YoY and WoW measures that use the date dimension’s week and prior-period keys **so that** comparisons remain correct when a week spans a month boundary.
- **Maps to:** Semantic model (DAX)
- **Delivers:** FR5
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - `Units YoY`, `Gross YoY`, `Net YoY` (and % change) using `prior_year_date` / parallel period — not calendar-month shift.
  - `Units WoW`, `Gross WoW`, `Net WoW` using `week_key` / `prior_week_date`; a week spanning two months is one bucket.
  - Totals and visual-level date filters respect the same week definition; tested on a known spanning week.

### US-4.3 Loyalty split & promotion effectiveness measures
**As a** marketing analyst, **I want** measures that split every core metric by loyalty vs guest and that compare category sales in a promo window vs a comparable baseline **so that** FR3 and FR4 can be reported without custom DAX in each visual.
- **Maps to:** Semantic model (DAX + calculation groups or helper tables as needed)
- **Delivers:** FR3, FR4
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - `Is Loyalty` (member vs guest) available as a dimension and as filtered measures; all core + time-intel measures filterable by it (FR4).
  - Promo effectiveness: for a selected `dim_promotion` (or promo_type + category), **In-window sales** vs **Baseline sales** for the same category. Baseline rule documented (e.g. equal-length period immediately before `start_date`, or prior-year aligned weeks) and implemented as measures (`Promo Sales`, `Baseline Sales`, `Uplift`, `Uplift %`).
  - Baseline excludes other overlapping promos on that category or flags them (rule in AC test cases).
  - Works with user-selected date range and does not double-count lines.

---

## Phase 5 — Power BI reporting & handover
*Thin reports on the semantic model. Each story is a shippable slice of the FR set.*

### US-5.1 Sales performance report (store / region / category)
**As a** regional manager, **I want** an interactive report of units, gross, and net by store, region, and product category over any date range **so that** I can see where sales landed (FR1) with returns visible separately (FR2).
- **Maps to:** Power BI on the semantic model
- **Delivers:** FR1, FR2, FR5
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Slicers: date range, region, store, category, loyalty vs guest.
  - Matrix / charts: Units, Gross, Returns, Net; drill store → category (and reverse).
  - Optional YoY / WoW toggle on the same page (FR5).
  - Date range is user-selected; no hard-coded period.
  - Performance: page interactive on 3 years at category/store grain.

### US-5.2 Promotion effectiveness report
**As a** category / marketing analyst, **I want** a report that compares category sales inside a promotion window with the agreed baseline **so that** I can judge promo lift (FR3), sliced by loyalty vs guest (FR4).
- **Maps to:** Power BI
- **Delivers:** FR3, FR4
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Select promo (or category + date) → see In-window vs Baseline vs Uplift for Units / Gross / Net.
  - Split by loyalty vs guest; optional store/region breakout.
  - Promo window and baseline period displayed as captions (auditability).
  - Matches semantic-model measures (no visual-level DAX that diverges).

### US-5.3 Daily operations & trust
**As a** analytics product owner, **I want** the end-to-end refresh (Pipeline → Notebooks → semantic model → reports) to run daily with observable freshness and a 3-year history **so that** the business can trust the numbers every morning (FR6).
- **Maps to:** Data Pipelines (orchestration), Lakehouse, semantic model refresh, Power BI
- **Delivers:** FR6 (regression check on FR1–FR5)
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Single orchestrated daily run; Gold and model watermark = previous business day (SLA agreed).
  - Failure / late-data alert to the ops channel; last-refresh visible on every report.
  - Reconciliation dashboard or notebook: Bronze vs Silver vs Gold vs report totals for a fixed test day.
  - Three years selectable in the date slicer; older partitions not required in v1.

---

## Traceability matrix (FR → stories)

| FR | Meaning | Stories |
|----|---------|---------|
| FR1 | Sales by store, region, category, date range | 1.2, 1.3, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 3.2, 3.3, 4.1, 5.1 |
| FR2 | Returns separate; net = gross − returns | 1.2, 2.1, 3.3, 4.1, 5.1 |
| FR3 | Promo window vs baseline | 1.3, 2.3, 3.2, 3.3, 4.3, 5.2 |
| FR4 | Loyalty vs guest | 1.2, 1.3, 2.1, 2.3, 3.2, 3.3, 4.3, 5.1, 5.2 |
| FR5 | YoY / WoW, weeks spanning months | 1.2, 3.1, 4.2, 5.1 |
| FR6 | Daily refresh, 3-year retain | 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1, 3.3, 4.1, 5.3 |

**Suggested sprint packaging:** Phase 1 = Sprint 1; Phase 2 = Sprint 2; Phase 3 = Sprint 3; Phase 4 = Sprint 4; Phase 5 = Sprint 5 (US-5.3 starts in Sprint 1 as a thin pipeline skeleton and is only *accepted* when reports are live).

haiku-4-5.text:
# Microsoft Fabric Analytics Roadmap: POS & Loyalty Analytics

---

## PHASE 1: DATA INGESTION & BRONZE LAYER (Sprint 1–2)

### Story 1.1: Ingest daily POS transaction headers
**As a** data engineer, **I want** to automatically ingest daily POS transaction files (pos_transactions) into a Lakehouse Bronze zone **so that** we have a reliable, timestamped archive of all receipt activity.

**Functional Requirement:** FR6 (daily refresh, 3-year history)

**Fabric Components:**
- **OneLake** (Lakehouse – Bronze folder)
- **Data Pipeline** with scheduled Copy Activity (daily trigger, 02:00 UTC)
- Source: ADLS → Target: Lakehouse Bronze table `pos_transactions_raw`

**Medallion Layer:** Bronze

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Pipeline ingests all daily files without error; failed runs alert via email
- [ ] Bronze table contains raw columns: `store_id, txn_ts, loyalty_id, channel, _load_date, _load_ts`
- [ ] Late-arriving data (same day) is handled via upsert; files older than 3 years are archived
- [ ] Data quality checks: row count ≥ threshold, no unexpected nulls in `store_id` or `txn_ts`
- [ ] SLA: 99% on-time completion within 4 hours of file availability

---

### Story 1.2: Ingest daily POS transaction line items
**As a** data engineer, **I want** to ingest POS line-item data (pos_lines) daily into Bronze **so that** we have granular sales detail (SKU, quantity, amounts, returns).

**Functional Requirement:** FR1, FR2 (sales units/gross/net, returns)

**Fabric Components:**
- **OneLake** (Lakehouse – Bronze folder)
- **Data Pipeline** (same schedule as Story 1.1)
- Source: ADLS → Target: Lakehouse Bronze table `pos_lines_raw`

**Medallion Layer:** Bronze

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Bronze table contains: `txn_id, sku, qty, gross_amount, discount_amount, return_flag, _load_date`
- [ ] Referential integrity check: all `txn_id` values exist in `pos_transactions_raw` (within 24 hours)
- [ ] Data validation: `qty ≥ 0`; `gross_amount ≥ 0`; `return_flag ∈ {0, 1}`
- [ ] Row count reconciliation: +/− 5% vs source system daily report
- [ ] SLA: 99% on-time within 4 hours

---

## PHASE 4: SEMANTIC MODELLING & POWER BI (Sprint 7–8)

### Story 4.1: Create Semantic Model (Power BI / Analysis Services)
**As a** BI architect, **I want** to build a semantic model on Fabric's Analysis Services backend **so that** Power BI reports have a consistent, governed metric layer**.

**Functional Requirement:** FR1–FR6 (all requirements depend on consistent metrics)

**Fabric Components:**
- **Semantic Model** (Power BI, hosted in Fabric)
- **OneLake** (Gold layer tables as sources)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Data source connections: to Gold tables in Lakehouse (OneLake)
- [ ] Fact tables: `fact_sales` (grain: line item), `fact_sales_agg_day_store_product`, `fact_sales_agg_week_store_category`, `fact_promotion_effectiveness`
- [ ] Dimension tables: `dim_date, dim_store, dim_product, dim_loyalty_member, dim_promotion`
- [ ] Relationships (star schema):
  - `fact_sales → dim_date` on `txn_date_key`
  - `fact_sales → dim_store` on `store_key`
  - `fact_sales → dim_product` on `product_key`
  - `fact_sales → dim_loyalty_member` on `loyalty_key`
  - `fact_sales → dim_promotion` on `promotion_key` (mark as inactive for many-to-one due to multiple promos per date)
- [ ] Measures (DAX):
  - **Sales Measures:**
    - `Total Gross Sales = SUM(fact_sales[gross_amount])`
    - `Total Discount = SUM(fact_sales[discount_amount])`
    - `Total Net Sales = SUM(fact_sales[net_amount])`
    - `Total Units Sold = SUM(fact_sales[units])`
  - **Return Measures:**
    - `Total Returns (Units) = SUMX(FILTER(fact_sales, fact_sales[is_return]=1), fact_sales[units])`
    - `Total Returns (Amount) = SUMX(FILTER(fact_sales, fact_sales[is_return]=1), fact_sales[net_amount])`
    - `Return Rate % = DIVIDE([Total Returns (Units)], [Total Units Sold], 0) * 100`
  - **Loyalty Measures:**
    - `Loyalty Sales = CALCULATE([Total Net Sales], dim_loyalty_member[segment] <> "Guest")`
    - `Guest Sales = CALCULATE([Total Net Sales], dim_loyalty_member[segment] = "Guest")`
    - `Loyalty % = DIVIDE([Loyalty Sales], [Total Net Sales], 0)`
  - **YoY & WoW Measures:**
    - `Net Sales YoY = CALCULATE([Total Net Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(dim_date[calendar_date]))`
    - `YoY Growth % = DIVIDE([Total Net Sales] - [Net Sales YoY], [Net Sales YoY], 0) * 100`
    - `Net Sales PriorWeek = CALCULATE([Total Net Sales], FILTER(ALL(dim_date), dim_date[date_key] = MAX(dim_date[prior_week_date_key])))`
    - `WoW Growth % = DIVIDE([Total Net Sales] - [Net Sales PriorWeek], [Net Sales PriorWeek], 0) * 100`
  - **Promotion Measures:**
    - `Promo Lift % = DIVIDE(SUM(fact_promotion_effectiveness[lift_net_amount_pct]), COUNTA(fact_promotion_effectiveness[promotion_key]), 0)`
- [ ] Row-Level Security (optional): by store region (dim_store[region])
- [ ] Aggregations: point aggregation to `fact_sales_agg_day_store_product` and `fact_sales_agg_week_store_category` for performance
- [ ] Query folding: verified in Power Query for all transformations
- [ ] Refresh schedule: daily (aligned with data pipeline in Phase 1)

  - Promotion date ranges align with source (spot check)
  - Loyalty member count = source (±0%)
- [ ] **Aggregate validation:**
  - `fact_sales_agg_day_store_product` sums reconcile to `fact_sales` (±0.01%)
  - `fact_sales_agg_week_store_category` sums reconcile to `fact_sales` (±0.01%)
  - Week boundaries crossing months correctly included
- [ ] **Time-based validation:**
  - YoY comparisons: same calendar day last year returns correct data ✓
  - WoW comparisons: same day-of-week last week returns correct data ✓
  - Date dimension coverage: all business dates in 3-year period present
- [ ] **Completeness:**
  - No missing days in daily refresh (alert if gap > 1 day)
  - Latest 3 years of data fully loaded
- [ ] All checks passed; sign-off from data steward

---

### Story 5.2: Performance & Scalability Testing
**As a** DevOps engineer, **I want** to validate that the solution meets performance SLAs **so that** production use is stable**.

**Functional Requirement:** FR6 (daily refresh), reporting responsiveness

**Fabric Components:**
- **Notebook** (load testing)
- **Power BI** (report execution tests)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] **Pipeline performance:**
  - Daily ingestion (all 6 sources) completes within 4 hours ✓
  - Transformation (Phase 2) completes within 30 minutes ✓
  - Gold table build (Phase 3) completes within 15 minutes ✓
  - End-to-end: < 5 hours, leaving 19-hour buffer before next run
- [ ] **Semantic Model:**
  - Semantic model size: < 2 GB (estimated for 3 years POS + masters)
  - Refresh time: < 30 minutes
- [ ] **Power BI Reports:**
  - All report visuals render within 2 seconds on filter apply ✓
  - Drill-through: < 1 second
  - Aggregate tables used (no full fact table scans)
- [ ] **Scalability (future-proofing):**
  - Test with 5 years of data (2× current volume): pipeline still meets SLA ✓
  - Test with 50 additional stores (3× current): same ✓
- [ ] Load test results documented; optimization opportunities flagged

---

### Story 5.3: User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
**As a** business user, **I want** to validate that reports answer my business questions **so that** I can confidently use the solution**.

**Functional Requirement:** FR1–FR6 (business requirements)

**Fabric Components:**
- **Power BI Reports** (all 5 from Phase 4)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] **Functional UAT:**
  - Test scenario FR1: Sales by store/region/category/date range returns expected results ✓
  - Test scenario FR2: Returns are shown separately; net = gross - discount ✓
  - Test scenario FR3: Promotion lift calculation matches manual sample ✓
  - Test scenario FR4: Loyalty vs guest segmentation is correct ✓
  - Test scenario FR5: YoY and WoW comparisons match manual calculation ✓
  - Test scenario FR6: Latest refresh time is current day; 3-year history available ✓
- [ ] **Usability:**
  - Filters work intuitively (date range picker, multi-select slicers)
  - Drill-through paths are logical
  - Export to PDF/Excel functions work
  - Mobile layout is usable
- [ ] **Sign-off:**
  - Business Sponsor: all requirements satisfied ✓
  - Operations Lead: ready for production ✓
  - Finance Lead: numbers reconcile to GL ✓

---

### Story 5.4: Documentation & Knowledge Transfer
**As a** support analyst, **I want** to have complete documentation and training materials **so that** the team can maintain and evolve the solution**.

**Functional Requirement:** FR6 (operational continuity)

**Fabric Components:**
- **Fabric Workspace** (documentation via notebooks, wiki)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] **Data Lineage & Metadata:**
  - Data dictionary: all Bronze, Silver, Gold tables documented (purpose, columns, grain, refresh frequency)
  - Lineage diagram: source → Bronze → Silver → Gold → Semantic Model → Reports (Visio or Miro)
  - Mapping document: source column → target column (per CSV mapping input)
- [ ] **Pipeline & Transformation Logic:**
  - Pipeline run book: trigger schedule, dependencies, error handling, alerting
  - Dataflow/Notebook logic documented: transformation rules, business logic, edge cases
  - SCD logic for dim_store documented with examples
- [ ] **Semantic Model:**
  - Measure definitions (DAX code & plain-English description)
  - Relationship diagram (star schema visual)
  - Performance tuning notes (aggregation usage)
- [ ] **Reports:**
  - Report user guide: how to use filters, interpret metrics, download data
  - Business rule documentation: what each metric means, calculation method
  - Known limitations & assumptions
- [ ] **Operations Manual:**
  - Monitoring & alerting setup: failed pipelines, data quality failures
  - Troubleshooting guide: common issues & resolutions
  - Escalation contacts
- [ ] **Training Materials:**
  - Video walk-through of each report (5–10 min each)
  - Q&A document for end users
- [ ] All stakeholder groups (Operations, Finance, Marketing, Merchandising, Pricing) trained and signed off

---

### Story 5.5: Cut-over & Production Go-Live
**As a** program manager, **I want** to execute a controlled transition to production **so that** business operations are not disrupted**.

**Functional Requirement:** FR6 (daily refresh, operational continuity)

**Fabric Components:**
- **Fabric Workspace** (production environment)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] **Pre-Go-Live:**
  - All previous stories (5.1–5.4) completed and signed off ✓
  - Parallel run: Fabric reports vs legacy system for 1 week; reconciliation ✓
  - Communication: go-live date, cutover plan, rollback plan communicated to all users
- [ ] **Go-Live Day:**
  - Morning: verify all pipelines scheduled and ready ✓
  - 02:00 UTC: first production refresh run; monitor closely ✓
  - Monitor dashboard created (Fabric Workspace health tile)
  - On-call support team briefed
- [ ] **Post-Go-Live (Day 1–7):**
  - Daily check: pipelines complete on time, no data anomalies
  - User feedback collection: any usability issues?
  - Performance monitoring: dashboard query times, semantic model refresh times
  - Support ticket triage: prioritize bug fixes vs enhancements
- [ ] **Stabilization (Week 2–4):**
  - Weekly reconciliation vs source system
  - Optimization: query performance tuning if needed
  - Documentation updates based on lessons learned
- [ ] **Sign-Off:**
  - Sponsor: solution meets all requirements ✓
  - Operations: confident in ongoing maintenance ✓
  - Finance: numbers certified ✓

---

## CROSS-CUTTING CONCERNS (All Sprints)

### Security & Governance
- **Row-Level Security:** Power BI report access restricted by region (optional, per Story 4.1)
- **Data Retention:** Bronze layer: 3 years rolling; archive older data to cold storage
- **Access Control:** OneLake folders restricted by role (Ingestion Admins, Transformers, Report Consumers)
- **Auditing:** data lineage captured via Fabric Purview; data access logged

### Monitoring & Alerting
- **Pipeline Health:**
  - Email alert on failed runs (recipient: DataOps mailing list)
  - Slack notification on 4+ hour delay
  - Dashboard tile: "Last refresh timestamp" — red if > 25 hours old
- **Data Quality:**
  - Row count variance > 10% from expected → alert
  - Null checks (store_id, txn_ts, sku) failures → quarantine + alert
  - Reconciliation variance > threshold → alert
- **Performance:**
  - Semantic model refresh > 60 minutes → alert
  - Power BI report query > 5 seconds → flag for optimization
  - Lakehouse size growth > 20% MoM → investigate

---

kimi-k3.text:
# Fabric Analytics Delivery Roadmap — Retail Sales & Promotions

**Story key:** each story shows its ID, the standard story format, the Fabric components, the medallion layer, and the functional requirements it delivers (`Delivers:` / `Supports:`). Assumes two-week sprints; adjust cadence as needed.

## Roadmap at a glance

| Phase | Sprint(s) | Theme | Medallion layer | FRs advanced |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | Platform foundation | — | Enabler for all |
| 1 | 1–2 | Ingestion | Bronze | FR6 (underpins all) |
| 2 | 3 | Cleansing & conformance | Silver | FR1, FR2, FR3, FR4 |
| 3 | 4–5 | Star schema & semantic model | Gold | FR1–FR6 |
| 4 | 6 | Reporting | Gold → Power BI | FR1–FR5 |
| 5 | 7 | Operationalise & validate | All | FR6 (+ full UAT) |

---

## Phase 0 — Foundation (Sprint 0)

**US-01 — Workspace, Lakehouse and environments**
*As a platform engineer, I want a Fabric workspace with a schema-enabled Lakehouse (bronze/silver/gold schemas) and a dev→test→prod deployment pipeline, so that all build work happens in a governed, promotable structure.*
**Fabric:** Workspace, Lakehouse on OneLake, deployment pipelines. **Supports:** all FRs.
- Lakehouse exists with bronze/silver/gold schemas; naming standards documented.
- Deployment pipeline promotes artefacts between environments.
- Access roles set (contributors vs viewers); no personal accounts on shared artefacts.

**US-02 — Secured source connectivity**
*As a data engineer, I want a secured, read-only connection to the source ADLS container, so that pipelines can consume the daily drops without embedded credentials.*
**Fabric:** Connections/gateways, workspace identity. **Supports:** all FRs.
- Connection authenticates via workspace identity/service principal; no keys in plain text.
- Read-only access verified against the POS drop folder and extract locations.

---

## Phase 1 — Ingestion to Bronze (Sprints 1–2)

*Exit: all six sources landing reliably in OneLake as raw, auditable Delta tables.*

**US-10 — Daily POS file ingestion**
*As a data engineer, I want the daily pos_transactions and pos_lines ADLS drops copied into bronze Delta tables by a scheduled Data Pipeline, so that downstream layers always have complete, auditable raw data.*
**Fabric:** Data Pipeline (Copy activity/Copy job) → Lakehouse bronze schema. **Delivers:** FR6. **Supports:** FR1, FR2, FR4, FR5.
- Pipeline runs daily after the drop window; files appended with `source_file` and `load_ts` metadata.
- Re-running a day is idempotent (no duplicate rows).
- File-vs-bronze row counts reconciled and logged; failure raises an alert.

**US-11 — Three-year historical load**
*As a data engineer, I want the ~3 years of historical POS files bulk-loaded into bronze, so that YoY comparisons and the 3-year retention requirement can be met from day one.*
**Fabric:** Data Pipeline (bulk copy) → bronze. **Delivers:** FR6. **Supports:** FR5.
- All historical files present; counts reconciled to source manifests.
- Load is partitioned/dated so retention policies can later target >36-month data.

**US-12 — Dimension extract ingestion**
*As a data engineer, I want product_master (weekly full extract) plus store_master, promotions and loyalty_members landed in bronze with snapshot preservation, so that conformed dimensions — including the store SCD — can be built.*
**Fabric:** Data Pipelines (weekly/on-demand schedules). **Supports:** FR1, FR3, FR4.
- product_master refreshes weekly; each full snapshot retained (enables change detection for SCD2).
- store_master, promotions, loyalty_members landed with `load_ts`; counts logged.

---

## Phase 2 — Transformation to Silver (Sprint 3)

*Exit: typed, deduplicated, conformed tables; a Type-2 store dimension; data quality enforced.*

**US-20 — Cleanse and conform POS facts**
*As an analytics engineer, I want silver tables where pos_lines are typed and deduplicated and joined to their headers (txn_ts, store_id, channel, loyalty_id), with return_flag standardised to a boolean is_return, so that the gold fact is built on trusted rows.*
**Fabric:** Spark notebook (Delta MERGE). **Delivers:** FR1, FR2. **Supports:** FR4.
- Grain of one row per txn_id + sku enforced; duplicates resolved per documented rule.
- Orphan lines (no header) quarantined with a DQ report (< agreed threshold).
- Null loyalty_id preserved (drives guest classification in FR4); is_return is strictly boolean.

**US-21 — Store dimension as SCD Type 2**
*As an analytics engineer, I want store_master maintained as an effective-dated Type-2 dimension, so that sales are attributed to the region a store belonged to **at the time of each transaction** (per the store region mapping).*
**Fabric:** Spark notebook (MERGE into silver store dimension). **Delivers:** FR1. **Supports:** FR5.
- A region re-assignment closes the current row and opens a new one; no overlapping effective dates.
- A historical point-in-time query returns the correct region for a known re-regioned store.

**US-22 — Conform product, loyalty and promotions**
*As an analytics engineer, I want product, loyalty and promotion tables cleansed in silver (valid keys, valid date ranges, deduplicated), so that gold dimensions and the promotion date-range join are reliable.*
**Fabric:** Dataflow Gen2 (low-volume dims) with DQ rules. **Delivers:** FR3, FR4. **Supports:** FR1.
- sku and loyalty_id unique; promo start_date ≤ end_date enforced.
- Overlapping promotions on the same category are detected and flagged for the precedence rule (US-32).

---

## Phase 3 — Gold Star Schema & Semantic Model (Sprints 4–5)

*Exit: a governed star schema in gold, surfaced through a Direct Lake semantic model with certified measures.*

**US-30 — fact_sales and core dimensions**
*As an analytics engineer, I want a gold star schema — fact_sales at receipt-line grain with dim_store (SCD2), dim_product, dim_customer and dim_date — populated exactly per the source-to-target mapping, so that reporting has a single governed source.*
**Fabric:** Spark notebook → gold Delta tables. **Delivers:** FR1, FR2, FR4.
- Mappings applied verbatim: qty→units, gross_amount→gross_amount, discount_amount→discount_amount, return_flag→is_return; region and category resolved via dims.
- Null loyalty_id maps to a single "Guest" row in dim_customer (from loyalty_members); fact row counts tie to silver.

**US-31 — Retail calendar for YoY/WoW**
*As a BI developer, I want a dim_date with a retail week calendar (e.g. 4-4-5) whose week index runs continuously across month boundaries, plus a prior-year comparable-week mapping, so that WoW and YoY comparisons are correct even for boundary-spanning weeks.*
**Fabric:** Notebook-generated gold dim_date. **Delivers:** FR5. **Supports:** FR1.
- Every date maps to one retail week; a week spanning a month-end aggregates all 7 days in both periods.
- Prior-year week resolves via 364-day (52-week) shift; calendar covers 3 years of history + current year.

**US-32 — Promotion attribution on the fact**
*As an analytics engineer, I want each fact row resolved to a promotion_key via the specified date-range join (category + txn date within promo window), with a documented precedence rule for overlapping promos, so that promo effectiveness is measurable.*
**Fabric:** Spark notebook during gold build → dim_promotion + fact promotion_key. **Delivers:** FR3.
- promos map per spec (promo_id → promotion_key); non-promo rows carry "No promotion".
- Overlaps resolved by the agreed rule (e.g. latest start_date wins) and logged; match rate per category reported.

**US-33 — Promotion baseline windows**
*As a BI developer, I want each promotion to carry a defined comparable baseline window (default: equal-length period immediately preceding; optional year-ago), so that promo-vs-baseline comparisons are consistent across reports.*
**Fabric:** Gold promo calendar table. **Delivers:** FR3.
- Baseline start/end stored per promotion; method switchable.
- Baselines that overlap other promotions are flagged so uplift isn't contaminated.

**US-34 — Semantic model with certified measures**
*As a BI developer, I want a Direct Lake semantic model over the gold tables with DAX measures — Units, Gross Sales, Returns, Net Sales (= Gross − Returns), Discounts, YoY/WoW deltas, Member/Guest split — so that every report uses consistent, certified KPIs.*
**Fabric:** Semantic model (Direct Lake; Import + incremental refresh as fallback). **Delivers:** FR1, FR2, FR4, FR5. **Supports:** FR3, FR6.
- Net = Gross − Returns verified against source totals for sample periods (±0.01 tolerance).
- Member + Guest equals total for every measure; YoY/WoW validated on a known boundary week.

---

## Phase 4 — Reporting (Sprint 6)

*Exit: four Power BI reports/pages covering FR1–FR5, all on the certified semantic model.*

**US-40 — Sales performance report**
*As a store operations manager, I want units, gross, returns (shown separately) and net by store, region and category over any selected date range, so that I can track trading performance.*
**Fabric:** Power BI on semantic model. **Delivers:** FR1, FR2.
- Date-range slicer drives all visuals; returns displayed as a distinct measure alongside net.
- Report totals reconcile to semantic model and to a finance-approved source sample.

**US-41 — Promotion effectiveness report**
*As a category manager, I want category sales in each promotion window compared to its baseline (absolute and % uplift), so that I can judge which promotions work.*
**Fabric:** Power BI + gold promo calendar. **Delivers:** FR3.
- Uplift validated by hand-calculation on one sample promotion; drill-through to store/region works.

**US-42 — Loyalty segmentation**
*As a CRM analyst, I want every measure splittable by member vs guest (and by member segment), so that I can quantify loyalty behaviour.*
**Fabric:** Power BI + dim_customer. **Delivers:** FR4.
- Member/guest/segment slicer works on all pages; split always sums to the total.

**US-43 — Trend comparison report**
*As a commercial analyst, I want YoY and WoW trend views that handle weeks spanning month ends, so that momentum comparisons are accurate.*
**Fabric:** Power BI + dim_date retail calendar. **Delivers:** FR5.
- A selected boundary-spanning week returns 7 full days for both current and prior-year periods; % change validated on a sample.

---

## Phase 5 — Operationalise & Validate (Sprint 7)

**US-50 — Orchestrated daily refresh with monitoring**
*As a data engineer, I want the end-to-end chain (pipeline → silver → gold → semantic model) orchestrated daily with failure alerts, so that reports are current before business open and issues are caught proactively.*
**Fabric:** Pipeline orchestration (notebook/dataflow activities), Activator alerts, monitoring hub. **Delivers:** FR6.
- Dependency chain runs daily; on-time completion logged; failures alert via Teams/email.
- Documented rerun/recovery procedure.

**US-51 — Retention management**
*As a data engineer, I want retention enforced so exactly 3 years of fact history is served (older data archived per policy), so that FR6 is met without unbounded growth.*
**Fabric:** Delta partitioning, table maintenance jobs. **Delivers:** FR6. **Supports:** FR5.
- Data older than 36 months removed/archived automatically; YoY still functions across the retention boundary.

**US-52 — UAT and sign-off**
*As a business analyst, I want a UAT pack reconciling report KPIs against source extracts for agreed sample periods, so that the business signs off the numbers with confidence.*
**Delivers:** FR1–FR6 (validation).
- Each FR has a demonstrated UAT script; reconciliation within tolerance; sign-off recorded.

---

## Traceability matrix

| FR | Delivered by stories | Validated in |
|---|---|---|
| FR1 — Sales by store/region/category, any date range | US-10, 11, 12, 20, 21, 30, 34, 40 | US-40, US-52 |
| FR2 — Returns separate; net = gross − returns | US-10, 20, 30, 34, 40 | US-34, US-40 |
| FR3 — Promo window vs baseline | US-12, 22, 32, 33, 41 | US-41 |
| FR4 — Member vs guest segmentation | US-12, 20, 22, 30, 34, 42 | US-42 |
| FR5 — YoY/WoW incl. month-boundary weeks | US-11, 21, 31, 34, 43, 51 | US-43 |
| FR6 — Daily refresh; 3-yr retention | US-10, 11, 34, 50, 51 | US-50, 51, 52 |

## Key assumptions & decisions

- **Net definition:** per FR2, Net = Gross − Returns; discount_amount is surfaced as its own measure (net-after-discount can be added without re-work).
- **Calendar:** 4-4-5 retail weeks recommended for FR5; ISO-8601 possible if the business prefers — decide in Sprint 4.
- **Promo overlaps:** precedence rule (e.g. latest start_date wins) to be confirmed with the category team during US-32.
- **Grain/key:** assumes pos_lines.txn_id → pos_transactions transaction key; guests = null loyalty_id.
- **Direct Lake** preferred for the semantic model (freshness without duplicate storage); Import with incremental refresh retained as fallback.

opus-5.text:
# Delivery Roadmap — Retail Sales Analytics on Microsoft Fabric

**Target architecture (one line):** ADLS daily drops → **Bronze** (Lakehouse Delta, raw + metadata) → **Silver** (conformed, historised, DQ-tested) → **Gold** (star schema: `fact_sales`, `dim_date`, `dim_store`, `dim_product`, `dim_customer`, `dim_promotion` + promo bridge) → **Direct Lake semantic model** → **Power BI reports**, all orchestrated by **Data Pipelines** on a daily schedule.

**Tooling convention used below:** Data Pipelines for ingestion/orchestration; **notebooks (PySpark)** for Silver/Gold transformation (chosen over Dataflow Gen2 for the fact-scale merges, SCD2 and range joins); **Dataflow Gen2** only for small, business-owned reference data; Lakehouse/OneLake for storage; Power BI for the semantic model and reports.

---

## Phase 0 — Foundations & Definitions (Sprint 0)

*Goal: environment exists, source access proven, and the ambiguous business rules are decided before any code is written.*

### S0.1 — Workspace, capacity and naming standards
**As a** Fabric platform engineer, **I want** DEV/TEST/PROD workspaces on a sized Fabric capacity with a Lakehouse per medallion layer and agreed naming standards, **so that** the build is deployable, cost-visible and consistent from day one.
- **FR trace:** enabler for all FRs (esp. FR6)
- **Fabric components:** Fabric capacity (F-SKU), 3 workspaces, Domain, `lh_bronze` / `lh_silver` / `lh_gold` Lakehouses, OneLake
- **Layer:** all
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Three workspaces exist, each assigned to capacity, with Contributor/Member/Viewer roles mapped to AAD groups (no individual grants).
  2. Bronze/Silver/Gold Lakehouses created in each workspace; naming standard documented (`bronze_<source>_<entity>`, `silver_<entity>`, `dim_*`/`fact_*`).
  3. Capacity sizing note records expected daily volume (3 yrs of POS lines) and the fallback plan if CU throttling occurs.
  4. Workspaces linked to Git (see S6.4) before first artefact is promoted.

### S0.2 — Source access and landing zone shortcut
**As a** data engineer, **I want** governed read access to the ADLS Gen2 daily drop surfaced as a OneLake shortcut, **so that** I can ingest without copying data twice or storing credentials in code.
- **FR trace:** FR6
- **Fabric components:** OneLake shortcut to ADLS Gen2, Lakehouse `Files/landing`, Azure Key Vault–backed connection
- **Layer:** Bronze (landing)
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Shortcut `lh_bronze/Files/landing/<source>/` resolves and lists files for all six sources.
  2. Authentication uses a service principal / managed identity; no secrets in notebooks or pipelines.
  3. File naming and arrival-time SLA documented per source (daily: POS; weekly: product_master).
  4. A read test on one day of `pos_lines` completes and row counts are logged.

### S0.3 — Metric, grain and business-rule definition workshop
**As a** business analyst, **I want** signed-off definitions for units, gross, discount, returns, net, "business date", and loyalty vs guest, **so that** every downstream layer computes the same numbers and rework is avoided.
- **FR trace:** FR1, FR2, FR4
- **Fabric components:** documented in a Lakehouse `/docs` folder + semantic model descriptions
- **Layer:** design artefact
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. `net = gross_amount − discount_amount − returns` (or the agreed variant) is written down with a worked example.
  2. Decision recorded on whether returns are separate rows flagged by `return_flag` with **positive** amounts (recommended) or negative amounts; a sign convention is chosen and is unambiguous.
  3. "Business date" defined: derived from `txn_ts` converted to **store local date** (not UTC), because a store's trading day drives store/region reporting.
  4. Loyalty vs guest defined as `loyalty_id IS NOT NULL` → member, else guest; guests are reported as a single explicit "Guest" member, never as blanks.
  5. Fact grain confirmed as **one row per receipt line** (`txn_id` + line), and the aggregation rules for units on return lines are stated.

### S0.4 — Promotion attribution and baseline rules
**As a** category manager, **I want** an agreed rule for attributing a sale to a promotion and an agreed definition of the "comparable baseline period", **so that** promotion effectiveness numbers are defensible and reproducible.
- **FR trace:** FR3
- **Fabric components:** design artefact, implemented later in S2.6 / S4.5
- **Layer:** design artefact
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Attribution rule documented: a line joins a promotion where `dim_product.category = promotions.category` **and** business date between `start_date` and `end_date` (inclusive).
  2. **Overlap rule decided** for the case where 2+ promotions match the same category/date (a real risk in this data): either (a) many-to-many via a bridge table so sales are not double counted in totals, or (b) a deterministic single-winner rule (e.g. latest `start_date`, then lowest `promo_id`). Choice and rationale recorded.
  3. Baseline definition chosen from: equal-length window immediately before the promo (excluding other promos in that category), or same window prior year. Chosen default plus at least one selectable alternative.
  4. Rule for non-promoted sales stated: they attribute to a "No Promotion" member key.

### S0.5 — Source profiling and data quality baseline
**As a** data analyst, **I want** a profile of each source (volumes, null rates, key uniqueness, orphan rates, date ranges), **so that** transformation rules and DQ thresholds are based on evidence rather than assumption.
- **FR trace:** FR6 (and de-risks FR1–FR5)
- **Fabric components:** Fabric notebook (PySpark) writing profile results to `lh_bronze`
- **Layer:** Bronze
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Profile report per source: row count, min/max date, null % per column, distinct key count vs row count.
  2. `pos_lines.txn_id` orphan rate against `pos_transactions` quantified; `loyalty_id` null rate quantified (drives FR4 expectations).
  3. Number of `store_id` values whose `region` has changed across snapshots is quantified — confirms the SCD2 requirement.
  4. Confirmed that 3 years of history is actually available in the drop location (FR6 retention target is achievable).

## Phase 1 — Bronze: Ingestion & Historisation (Sprints 1–2)

*Goal: every source lands in OneLake as Delta, incrementally, replayably, with lineage metadata. No business logic.*

### S1.1 — Daily incremental ingest of POS transactions and lines
**As a** data engineer, **I want** `pos_transactions` and `pos_lines` daily files copied into Bronze Delta tables with append-only, watermark-driven loads, **so that** sales data is available every day without full reloads.

- **Fabric components:** Data Pipeline (Copy activity + ForEach over file dates), Lakehouse `bronze_pos_transactions`, `bronze_pos_lines`
- **Layer:** Bronze

  1. Tables partitioned by ingest/business date; source columns retained as-is with original types where possible.
  2. Every row carries `_source_file`, `_ingested_at_utc`, `_pipeline_run_id`, `_batch_date`.
  3. Re-running the pipeline for the same file date produces no duplicates (idempotent: delete-partition-then-insert or MERGE on natural key).

  2. Two consecutive snapshots can be diffed by query to show changed `region` / `format` values.
  3Re-ingesting a snapshot date replaces only that partition.
  4. Snapshot retention covers the full 3-year reporting window (FR6).

### S1.3 — Weekly ingest of product_master

- **Layer:** Bronze

  1. Weekly snapshot loaded with `snapshot_date`; duplicate SKUs within a snapshot are reported as a DQ warning.

## Phase 2 — Silver: Conform, Cleanse, Historise (Sprints 3–4)

*Goal: business-ready, typed, deduplicated, historised entities with DQ gates. Still no star schema.*

### S2.1 — Conformed sales transaction lines
**As a** data engineer, **I want** a Silver `silver_sales_line` table joining receipt lines to their headers with typed columns and a derived store-local business date, **so that** all downstream reporting shares one trustworthy sales grain.
- **FR trace:** FR1, FR2, FR4, FR5
- **Fabric components:** Fabric notebook (PySpark) MERGE into `silver_sales_line` (Delta, partitioned by business date)
- **Layer:** Silver
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Grain = one row per receipt line; a uniqueness test on (`txn_id`, line identifier) passes.
  2. Header attributes carried down: `store_id`, `txn_ts`, `channel`, `loyalty_id` (nullable preserved).
  3. `business_date` derived per S0.3 (store-local) and never null.
  4. Numeric fields cast to decimal with agreed precision/scale; no float money.
  5. Lines with no matching header are routed to `silver_sales_line_rejects` with a reason code, and the reject rate is published.
  6. Load is incremental and idempotent for a re-run of any business date.

### S2.2 — Returns normalisation
**As a** finance analyst, **I want** returns identified consistently on every sales line with an agreed sign convention, **so that** gross, returns and net can be reported separately and always reconcile.
- **FR trace:** FR2, FR1
- **Fabric components:** notebook logic in `silver_sales_line`
- **Layer:** Silver
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. `is_return` boolean derived from `return_flag`, with the values-to-boolean mapping documented.
  2. `units`, `gross_amount`, `discount_amount` stored under the S0.3 convention consistently — a single query proves `sum(gross where not return) − sum(gross where return)` equals the agreed net-of-returns figure.
  3. Rows where `is_return = true` but amounts have the "wrong" sign are flagged as DQ exceptions.
  4. Returns are **not** filtered out of the fact — they remain queryable rows (FR2 requires separate visibility).

### S2.3 — Store dimension history (SCD Type 2)
**As a** regional manager, **I want** store attributes historised as SCD Type 2 with effective dates, **so that** a re-regioned store's past sales can be reported either under the region that owned them at the time or under today's region.
- **FR trace:** FR1, FR5
- **Fabric components:** notebook SCD2 MERGE over `bronze_store_master` snapshots → `silver_store_scd2`
- **Layer:** Silver
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Each store has non-overlapping, gapless `valid_from`/`valid_to` ranges with exactly one `is_current = true` row.
  2. A change to `region` or `format` closes the prior version and opens a new one; a change to nothing produces no new row (re-runs are stable).
  3. A test case using a known re-regioned store returns the correct region for a date before and after the change.
  4. Both "as-at" and "current" region are obtainable (current is exposed for default reporting; as-at is retained for restatement questions).

### S2.4 — Product and loyalty reference conformance
**As a** data engineer, **I want** conformed `silver_product` and `silver_loyalty_member` tables built from the latest snapshots with cleansed categories and segments, **so that** category and loyalty-segment reporting is stable.
- **FR trace:** FR1, FR3, FR4
- **Fabric components:** notebook or Dataflow Gen2 → `silver_product`, `silver_loyalty_member`
- **Layer:** Silver
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. One row per `sku` and one per `loyalty_id`; duplicates resolved by latest snapshot with a documented tie-break.
  2. Category/brand/segment values trimmed and case-standardised; a mapping table handles known renames so trends aren't broken.
  3. SKUs appearing in sales but absent from product_master are counted and default to an "Unknown Product" handling path (they must not disappear from sales totals).
  4. Product SCD approach recorded (Type 1 on category for v1, with a note on the impact on FR3 historic comparability).

### S2.5 — Promotion window resolution
**As a** data engineer, **I want** a resolved promotion-to-sales-line relationship built from the category + date-range join with the S0.4 overlap rule applied, **so that** promotion effectiveness can be measured without double counting sales.
- **FR trace:** FR3
- **Fabric components:** notebook range join → `silver_promo_line_bridge` (or resolved single `promo_id` on the line)
- **Layer:** Silver
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Join implemented as `category` equality **and** `business_date BETWEEN start_date AND end_date`.
  2. The overlap rule from S0.4 is enforced; a test with a deliberately overlapping promo pair produces the documented outcome.
  3. **Total sales measured through the promotion path equals total sales measured without it** (no fan-out inflation) — this is a hard test.
  4. Non-promoted lines are attributable to a "No Promotion" key.
  5. Promotion windows that change retrospectively can be reprocessed for affected date ranges.

### S2.6 — Data quality gates and reconciliation
**As a** data steward, **I want** automated DQ tests with severities that can block the Gold load, **so that** bad data is caught before it reaches reports and erodes trust.
- **FR trace:** FR6 (protects FR1–FR5)
- **Fabric components:** notebook test suite writing to `dq_results`, pipeline conditional (Fail/If activity), Power BI DQ page
- **Layer:** Silver → Gold gate
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Tests implemented for: row uniqueness at grain, not-null on keys/dates, referential integrity (line→header, line→product, line→store), amount reconciliation Bronze vs Silver, date-range sanity.
  2. Each test has a severity; **error**-severity failures stop the Gold load, **warning**-severity failures log and continue.
  3. Results are queryable by run date and surfaced on a DQ report page.
  4. Reconciliation totals (units, gross) between Bronze and Silver match to zero variance for the last 7 days.

## Phase 3 — Gold: Dimensional Model (Sprints 5–6)

*Goal: a conformed star schema in `lh_gold` designed for Direct Lake and for the specific comparison requirements FR3/FR5.*

### S3.1 — Date dimension with a week-aware calendar
**As a** reporting analyst, **I want** a `dim_date` covering 3+ years with ISO/retail week attributes, week-start dates and prior-year/prior-week alignment keys, **so that** week-on-week and year-on-year comparisons work correctly even when a week spans a month boundary.
- **FR trace:** FR5, FR1, FR6
- **Fabric components:** notebook-generated `dim_date` in `lh_gold`; marked as date table in the semantic model
- **Layer:** Gold
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Contiguous dates from (earliest sale − 1 yr) to (current year end); no gaps, one row per date.
  2. Attributes include `date_key`, calendar year/quarter/month, `iso_year_week`, `week_start_date`, `week_end_date`, `day_of_week`, plus retail 4-5-4 period if adopted.
  3. **Week hierarchy is independent of the month hierarchy** — a week spanning e.g. 29 Jan–4 Feb belongs to exactly one week key and is not split or double counted; a documented test case proves it.
  4. `prior_year_date` (date- or week-aligned per S0.3 decision) and `prior_week_date` columns exist so YoY/WoW does not rely on `SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR` alone.
  5. Flags for `is_current_week`, `is_complete_week`, `is_complete_month` so part-period comparisons can be excluded.

### S3.2 — Store, product and customer dimensions
**As a** reporting analyst, **I want** `dim_store`, `dim_product` and `dim_customer` with surrogate keys and explicit unknown/guest members, **so that** every fact row joins and no sales are lost from totals.
- **FR trace:** FR1 (store/region, category), FR4 (loyalty vs guest)
- **Fabric components:** notebooks → `dim_store`, `dim_product`, `dim_customer` in `lh_gold`
- **Layer:** Gold
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Each dimension has an integer/hash surrogate key, business key, and `-1` "Unknown" member.
  2. `dim_store` carries SCD2 versions from S2.3 (`store_sk`, `valid_from/to`, `is_current`) plus `region` and `format`; `region` maps from `store_master.region` per the CSV mapping.
  3. `dim_product` carries `category` and `brand` per the CSV mapping (`product_master.category → dim_product.category`).
  4. `dim_customer` contains one row per loyalty member (`loyalty_id`, `join_date`, `segment`) **plus a single "Guest" member** used for all null-loyalty transactions, and a `customer_type` column with values Member/Guest.
  5. No fact row fails to join to any dimension (tested at 0 orphans).

### S3.3 — Promotion dimension and bridge
**As a** category manager, **I want** `dim_promotion` plus the sales-to-promotion relationship, **so that** I can slice sales by promotion, promo type and window.
- **FR trace:** FR3
- **Fabric components:** `dim_promotion`, `bridge_sales_promotion` (if many-to-many) in `lh_gold`
- **Layer:** Gold
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. `promotions.promo_id → dim_promotion.promotion_key` per the CSV mapping, with `promo_type`, `category`, `start_date`, `end_date`, plus a "No Promotion" member.
  2. Promotion duration in days and a window identifier are pre-computed for baseline comparison.

### S3.4 — Sales fact table
**As a** reporting analyst, **I want** `fact_sales` at receipt-line grain with foreign keys to all dimensions and additive measures, **so that** I can report units, gross, discount and returns by any combination of store, region, category, customer type and date.
- **FR trace:** FR1, FR2, FR4, FR5
- **Fabric components:** notebook MERGE → `fact_sales` (Delta, partitioned by `date_key`, V-Order enabled), `lh_gold`
- **Layer:** Gold
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Columns per the CSV mapping: `units` ← `pos_lines.qty`; `gross_amount` ← `pos_lines.gross_amount`; `discount_amount` ← `pos_lines.discount_amount`; `is_return` ← `pos_lines.return_flag`.

  3. Grain uniqueness test passes; sum of `units`/`gross_amount` reconciles to Silver with zero variance.
  4. Incremental daily merge on business-date partitions; a re-run of any date is idempotent.
  5. Partitioning, file sizes and OPTIMIZE/V-Order verified as Direct Lake–friendly (no small-file explosion).

### S3.5 — Gold regression test pack

- **Layer:** Bronze/Silver/Gold
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. `fact_sales` and Silver sales retain exactly the rolling 3-year window plus current period, per the documented rule.
  2. Retention deletes are logged and reversible from Bronze/archive for at least the audit period.
  3. OPTIMIZE and VACUUM run on schedule; time-travel retention set deliberately (not left at default) and documented.
  4. Storage growth trend is reported monthly.

### S6.3 — Late-arriving data and restatement handling
**As a** finance analyst, **I want** late or corrected source files to be reprocessed for the affected dates and reported figures to be restated transparently, **so that** I can trust and explain changes in published numbers.
- **FR trace:** FR6, FR2, FR1
- **Fabric components:** parameterised reprocess pipeline, partition-level MERGE, audit table
- **Layer:** Bronze → Gold
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Reprocessing a past business date updates Silver and Gold for that date only, with no duplication and no impact on other dates.
  2. Restatements are logged (date, source, rows changed, amount delta) and visible to finance.
  3. Runbook covers "file arrived late", "file arrived wrong", "promotion window changed retrospectively", "store re-regioned retrospectively".

### S6.4 — ALM: Git, deployment pipelines, environments
**As a** delivery lead, **I want** all Fabric artefacts source-controlled and promoted DEV→TEST→PROD via deployment pipelines with parameterised connections, **so that** releases are repeatable and auditable.
- **FR trace:** enabler for all FRs
- **Fabric components:** Git integration, Fabric deployment pipelines, deployment rules/variable libraries
- **Layer:** all
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Notebooks, pipelines, semantic model and reports are in Git with branch/PR policy.
  2. A release can be promoted to PROD with connections/paths re-pointed automatically, with no manual edits.
  3. Rollback to the previous release is demonstrated.
  4. Release notes reference the stories and FRs delivered.

### S6.5 — Monitoring, SLA and support handover
**As a** service owner, **I want** an operational dashboard for freshness, run duration, DQ status and capacity usage, plus a support runbook, **so that** the platform can be run in BAU after the project closes.
- **FR trace:** FR6
- **Fabric components:** Monitoring hub, Capacity Metrics app, Power BI ops report over `ctl_load_audit` / `dq_results`, Activator alerts
- **Layer:** cross-cutting
- **Acceptance criteria**
  1. Ops dashboard shows last successful load per source, freshness vs SLA, DQ pass rate, run durations, capacity CU trend.
  2. Alerts defined for late load, failed load, DQ error-severity failure, capacity throttling.
  3. Runbook covers top failure modes with resolution steps and escalation path.
  4. Support team completes a shadow run and formally accepts the service.

---

## Traceability Matrix (FR → Stories)

| FR | Requirement | Delivered by |
|---|---|---|
| **FR1** | Sales (units, gross, net) by store, region, category over any date range | S0.3, S1.1–S1.3, S2.1, S2.3, S2.4, S3.1, S3.2, S3.4, S4.1, S4.2, S4.7, S5.1, S5.4 |
| **FR2** | Returns shown separately; net = gross − returns | S0.3, S2.1, S2.2, S3.4, S4.2, S5.1, S6.3 |
| **FR3** | Promotion effectiveness vs comparable baseline | S0.4, S1.4, S2.5, S3.3, S4.5, S5.2, S3.5 |
| **FR4** | Segment all measures by member vs guest | S0.3, S1.4, S2.4, S3.2 (Guest member), S4.3, S5.3 |
| **FR5** | YoY and WoW comparison incl. month-boundary weeks | S3.1 (week-aware `dim_date`), S4.4, S3.5, S5.1, S1.5 (≥2 yrs history) |
| **FR6** | Daily refresh; 3 years of history retained | S0.2, S0.5, S1.1–S1.6, S2.6, S6.1, S6.2, S6.3, S6.5 |

---

## Key Design Decisions & Risks to Resolve in Phase 0

1. **Returns sign convention (FR2).** The single biggest source of reconciliation disputes. Decide once in S0.3; the recommended pattern is positive amounts plus `is_return`, with netting done in DAX.
2. **Promotion fan-out (FR3).** A category+date-range join will multiply sales rows whenever two promotions overlap on the same category. The mapping in Input 2 does not specify a resolution rule — S0.4 must decide bridge vs single-winner, and S2.5 must prove totals are un-inflated.
3. **Store SCD2 vs reporting default (FR1).** Historised region is built (S2.3), but reports need a default: current region for like-for-like trend, as-at region for historical accountability. Choose the default and expose the other explicitly.
4. **Weeks vs months (FR5).** Weeks cannot be nested under months. `dim_date` must expose an independent week hierarchy and comparison measures must use week keys, not month context.
5. **Baseline comparability (FR3).** A naive "prior N days" baseline is contaminated by other promotions, seasonality and trading-day mix. Exclusions and the alternative prior-year baseline must be agreed with the category team, not assumed.
6. **Guest transactions (FR4).** `loyalty_id` is nullable; without an explicit Guest member, guest sales fall out of segmented totals. Enforce the `-1`/Guest pattern in `dim_customer`.
7. **Timezone / trading day (FR1, FR5).** `txn_ts` must be converted to store-local date, otherwise late-night sales shift days and distort WoW comparisons.
8. **Unknown SKUs / stores.** Sales referencing missing master data must route to Unknown members rather than being dropped — otherwise Gold totals will not reconcile to Bronze.
